anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: The denominator never shrinks. Every evaluated variant lands in the hash-chained ledger with a closed-vocabulary decision; kills are never deleted; the union-N across grid versions is served beside every family. (critical)
anti_goal_violations.evidence: INTRODUCED AND FIXED INSIDE THIS ITERATION (the iteration-2 pattern), found by the independent auditor after review and QA both passed the code. Two faults, both in the ledger contract this journey exists to guarantee: (B2) scout_ledger.py's chain walk could not detect a TAIL truncation - erasing the most recent kill row left verify_chain() reporting ok: True with variants_tried silently 3 -> 2; (B3) variants_tried_for_family counted ledger ROWS rather than distinct candidate_ids, so every re-run of the identical grid inflated the served union-N (and bricked POST /scout/compute at the 24-variant cap after 12 runs). Fixed by a durable chain_head.json tail anchor written after the row it commits to, plus scout_ledger.distinct_variant_count. VERIFIED FIXED BY THE EVALUATOR against live code, not read off the handoff: tail truncation now reads {'ok': False, 'failed_at_row': 12, 'reason': 'tail_truncated'}, and three consecutive identical grid runs grew the ledger 6 -> 12 -> 18 rows (every evaluation permanently on record, nothing suppressed) while variants_tried held at 2 per family.

anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: Referee-era / Rapid-Microscope screening honesty: no threshold, grid, formula, embargo, or fold parameter is chosen or revised from validation outcomes; the screening null must not be anti-conservative. (critical)
anti_goal_violations.evidence: INTRODUCED AND FIXED INSIDE THIS ITERATION. Audit B4: scout.py's _block_length_for_horizon returned a 20-event block for EVERY shares and clock horizon (documented in the dev handoff as 'a conservative floor' - it is the opposite). Spec section 5.3 requires block length >= the longest evaluated horizon's label span in events; a clock_seconds_300 horizon spans hundreds-to-thousands of trades, so the null was narrowed and p_screen anti-conservative on a callable path whose results are permanently ledgered. Section 5.3's non-overlapping anchor subsampling was also absent entirely and undisclosed. Fixed by REFUSING rather than inventing (T-1): a typed ScoutUnsupportedHorizonError raised at the registration boundary before any corpus read or ledger write. VERIFIED BY THE EVALUATOR: nothing this iteration registers is affected (the whole grid is trade-count-only, where block length equals the label span exactly), and 142 tests across the four touched test files pass. CARRY-FORWARD: restoring shares/clock horizons needs per-session block sizing PLUS the subsampling and its own calibration trap - real work for whichever journey first registers a clock-horizon candidate, never a patch.
